A guide to sourdough baking

Sourdough bread is made using a fermented starter instead of commercial yeast. The starter is a culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria that develops over days of regular feeding with flour and water.

A healthy starter doubles in size within four to six hours after feeding, and it smells pleasantly tangy rather than sharply acidic.

Bakers often keep their starters at room temperature during active baking weeks and refrigerate them when they are not in use.
